newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Q1 '97 cocoa grind up 20.74 pct vs Q1 1996.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Q1 '97 cocoa grind up 20.74 pct vs Q1 1996.

text.p: U.S. cocoa grindings rose sharply in first quarter 1997, surging 20.74 percent to 95,435 tonnes versus the same year-ago period, trading sources said.
The increase, which far surpassed industry forecasts for a modest rise in grindings, was expected to be bullish for CSCE cocoa futures.
"It should be bullish," a trader said. "It is more than most people expected."
CSCE cocoa rallied at the opening, with most-active July rising $20 to $1,471 a tonne by 0916 EDT. That surpassed the pre-opening call of up $5 to $10.
The first quarter 1997 grindings compared with a year-ago reading of 79,044 tonnes.
The quantity of liquor melted fell 4.23 percent on the year to 2,103 tonnes, while the total butter melted dropped 4.95 percent to 15,298 tonnes.
